title: chain and sprockets
description: A hand crank turns a big sprocket and a chain turns a small sprocket twice as fast; no bicycle, wheel or rider shown

facts.intro: Introduce a recognizable chain drive: a large brass sprocket with a red crank on the left, a small orange sprocket on the right and a steel chain looped around both. Everything is still.
facts.cutaway: A simplified cutaway lifts the cover to expose the chain links, the teeth of both sprockets and the crank on the big sprocket.
facts.drive: An illustrated push turns the crank and the big sprocket. Its teeth pull the chain along, and the chain spins the small sprocket.
facts.response: The chain keeps moving around the loop. The small sprocket has half as many teeth, so it makes two turns for every turn of the big one.
facts.hold: No part moves for this explanation. Every chain link sits in a tooth gap; the big sprocket has sixteen teeth and the small one has eight.
facts.repeat: A second push turns the big sprocket another full turn, and the small sprocket makes two more turns, still in the same direction.
facts.limit: The crank turns backwards for a moment. The chain runs backwards around the loop, and both sprockets reverse together.
facts.payoff: The cover closes. Crank, big sprocket, chain and small sprocket work together: one slow turn becomes two fast turns. No bicycle is shown.

narration_rules.message: no bicycle or wheel is depicted; speak only of the crank, sprockets and chain
